question: How many active New World screwworm cases will Mexico's Senasica dashboard report in late October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: national active count has oscillated 1,850-2,100 since September (1,905 early Sep, 1,880 Sep 13, ~2,055 late Sep, 2,025 wk41, 1,968 Oct 16, 1,976 Oct 17). Resolving report is ~10-14 days away. Seasonality: in 2025 new cases peaked in wk43 (late Oct), and Chihuahua/north is rising with rains, a mild upward pull; the 15-day reclassification cycle and the recent dip pull the other way. No market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi. Median ~1,985 with roughly ±160 at the 10/90 percentiles; I see no way for the count to leave 1,200-2,800 in two weeks.
sources: web search results on Sept 2026 national active counts (1,905; 1,880 Sep 13; 2,055)

calls.reasoning: The latest confirmed dashboard total is 1,976 (report of Oct 17); it was 1,968 a few days earlier. Since September the series has stayed between about 1,850 and 2,100, and the 15-day active window makes it persistent. One or two updates remain before Oct 31. The pull upward comes from rains in Chihuahua and the north, the fact that weekly new cases peaked in epidemiological week 43 in 2025, and new cases running about 10% higher after the sterile-fly releases began. The pull downward comes from the drift from the late-September peak of about 2,055, cooling in the north and the 15-day reclassification. The two roughly cancel, so the median stays near the latest value. I found no human market for this number.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the anchor (1,968–1,976), on the ~1,850–2,100 range and on the absence of a market. Their medians differ by only about 37 (1,948–1,985). One factual conflict remains: one run cites 2,025 for week 41 (Tierra Fuerte) while the others cite 1,968 (Oct 14/16) and 1,976 (Oct 17). I had no web access and could not settle it. The 2,025 figure may be a different cutoff or a mis-citation. Two sources agree on 1,976, so I anchor there, and the 2,025 figure is one reason I lean slightly up rather than down. Run 3's downward drift and Runs 1–2's seasonal upward pull are a judgment call. The 2025 week-43 peak in new cases is the best seasonal evidence available, while the September-to-October drift is small, so I put the median at the latest value. I see no plausible way for the total to leave 1,200–2,800 within about 11 days, so I declare no escape mass. I carry forward the runs' reference class and their volatility-based width of about 290.

disagreements.verdict: Could not settle without web access. Anchored on 1,976, which two sources support; the conflict adds slight upward uncertainty.
